summary: Configured node1 to boot with audit=1 persistently via grubby (updates BLS entry and /etc/kernel/cmdline), then rebooted the node to verify the kernel parameter survives a reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: AlmaLinux 9.6, BIOS boot, GRUB2 with BLS (GRUB_ENABLE_BLSCFG=true)
Captured baseline boot_id (31b01b46-96de-4ded-a021-49887e7d4053) and confirmed /proc/cmdline lacked audit=1
Ran `grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1"` to add the parameter to the kernel's boot entry
Verified the BLS entry file (/boot/loader/entries/*.conf) and /etc/kernel/cmdline both now include audit=1
Rebooted node1 via `systemctl reboot` (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was available again, confirming boot_id changed to 0d7d2b19-26bc-41ca-8fd5-f159df8143f3
Verified /proc/cmdline on the new boot includes audit=1, and system is fully running (systemctl is-system-running -> running)

evidence.summary: grubby added audit=1 to the kernel args; BLS entry and /etc/kernel/cmdline show audit=1; post-reboot /proc/cmdline confirms audit=1 is active on the running kernel

evidence.requirement: Setting persists across reboot (node1 restart evidence protocol)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id captured (31b01b46...) before reboot; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node was unreachable mid-reboot (timeout), then came back with a new boot_id (0d7d2b19...) and uptime reset, proving an actual restart occurred; post-restart /proc/cmdline retained audit=1 and system reports fully running
